answer: Bonded staking mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock cryptocurrency collateral to activate an identity. Rather than dispersing an untraceable nebula of bots, each agent must bind to a public trellis of bonded smart contracts. The verifiable cost per identity is the locked capital and its forfeited yield. A key limitation is that this rigid marble barrier prices out low-capital honest agents while allowing wealthy cartels to buy multiple identities.
